title: General Autonomy wins gold in India's first RobotDog race as quadruped PARAM clocks 4.3 m/s top speed
excerpt: Bengaluru-based robotics startup General Autonomy has won gold in India's first RobotDog race, as its quadrupedal robot, PARAM, secured the top position at the Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026. PARAM competed against robots developed by xTerra Robotics and Strider Robotics at the AI and Robotics Pavilion. Bharat1.ai organised the event as part of the technology summit, held from November 17 to 19. Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar flagged off the competition. The three robots raced over a 100-metre course, with General Autonomy emerging as the winner. PARAM also recorded a reported top speed of 4.3 metres per second, making it one of the key highlights of the event. About General Autonomy General Autonomy was founded in 2023 by IIT Kanpur alumnus Farid Ahsan and Bhanu Pratap Singh, both former senior executives at social media platform ShareChat. Ahsan previously served as ShareChat's Chief Operating Officer (COO), while Singh was its Chief Technology Officer (CTO). Both left their executive positions in January 2023 before venturing into robotics. General Autonomy raised $3 million (around Rs 25 crore) in its first funding round in November 2023. The round was led by India Quotient and Elevation Capital, with participation from angel investors, including ShareChat co-founder Ankush Sachdeva. The company is developing both quadrupedal and humanoid robots. Its product portfolio includes PARAM, a four-legged robot, and ATOM, a humanoid platform. What makes PARAM special? PARAM is designed to move across challenging terrain and perform tasks in environments that may be difficult for humans or conventional machines to access. According to the company's published specifications, the robot weighs around 50 kg and can carry a payload of up to 25 kg. It has 12 degrees of freedom, which help it move on four legs and navigate different surfaces. The company sees potential applications for PARAM in defence, industrial inspection, surveillance and payload delivery. Quadrupedal robots are particularly useful in locations where wheeled machines face mobility challenges. They can navigate uneven ground, stairs and other obstacles. xTerra Robotics and Strider Robotics also compete The race also featured two other Indian robotics startups. xTerra Robotics participated with its quadrupedal robot DHAV, which secured second place. The machine is designed for industrial inspection, security and surveillance. It can monitor facilities and collect information from locations that may be difficult for humans to access. Strider Robotics entered the competition with its M3 robot, which finished third. Initially developed for defence applications, M3 is also being explored for industrial surveillance, construction monitoring and security operations. It has a reported payload capacity of around 45 kg. Milestone for India's robotics industry The competition showcased the progress Indian startups are making in developing autonomous machines. These machines can understand their surroundings, navigate obstacles and perform tasks with varying degrees of human intervention. The field is often described as Physical AI, where artificial intelligence moves beyond screens and software to interact with the physical world. India's growing interest in this technology could open opportunities across defence, manufacturing, infrastructure, logistics and disaster response. “Backflips today. Breakthroughs tomorrow. Manifesting India’s first gold in Robot Olympics,” General Autonomy shared on LinkedIn with a practice video of PARAM a week back.

title: Drones, cryptocurrencies, radicalisation, AI misuse dominate anti-terror conference discussions
excerpt: New Delhi, Nov 20 (PTI): The use of drones to transport narcotics, arms and explosives, cryptocurrency-enabled terror financing, online radicalisation and misuse of artificial intelligence (AI) were among the key issues discussed at a two-day anti-terror conference that concluded here on Friday. Giving details of the discussions, National Investigation Agency (NIA) Director General Rakesh Aggarwal said the first technical session focussed on "organised crime and terrorism nexus", with particular emphasis on the threat posed by drones. "The challenge is that drones are a very low-cost but highly effective tool used for transporting narcotics, arms, cash and explosives," Aggarwal said. "Now, since it is low cost, even if you shoot it down, how many (would you shoot)? So I think it's an asymmetric kind of situation. So the challenge is how to block these drones," he added. He said the challenge was to develop an effective mechanism to prevent unauthorised drones from entering the country, similar to physical barriers that prevent people from crossing the border. Punjab has faced the maximum drone threat, with the highest number of drone crossings recorded in the state, the NIA chief said while briefing reporters after the conclusion of the anti-terror conference. The second session focused on radicalisation, particularly the use of online platforms to spread extremist content. Aggarwal highlighted the availability of radicalising material on platforms like Facebook, Meta, Telegram, Signal, besides other websites and open-source material. He said magazines and newsletters published by terrorist groups, along with glorification of their activities or exaggerated accounts of atrocities against some people, were also being projected on these platforms. "And of course there are other means of radicalisation. The radicalisation through physical means, gatherings, and prisons being used for networking, among others," the NIA DG said. The third session was on cross-border terror financing, with a focus on the challenges posed by cryptocurrencies, which are difficult to crack and can conceal the identities of senders and receivers without leaving any trail, Aggarwal said. The fourth session was on international cooperation on combating cross-border terrorism. He said India had achieved "good successes" in securing the return of fugitives from other countries and the number is increasing continuously. However, he underlined that there were a lot of challenges in securing international cooperation. "This is a very technical kind of a subject because we deal with how to get evidence from other countries and there are very formal mechanisms of mutual legal assistance requests and letters rogatory," he said. Discussions were held on how to use these channels more effectively, he added. Aggarwal said 303 fugitives had been brought back to India since 1999, including 72 so far this year. The corresponding figures were 69 in 2025, 43 in 2024, 37 in 2023, 40 in 2022, 23 in 2021, 8 in 2020 and 11 in 2019. The fifth session was on the use of technology in countering cross-border terror offences, particularly artificial intelligence. Discussions covered the use of AI by terrorist groups and law enforcement agencies "to counter propaganda" as well as challenges related to SIM cards, he said. Union Home Minister Amit Shah attended two technical sessions also -- one on the nexus between organised crime and terrorism and the other on the use of technology to counter cross-border terrorism, Aggarwal said. The sixth anti-terror conference organised by the NIA concluded with a renewed commitment to strengthening India's collective counter-terrorism architecture through closer coordination between central and state agencies, intelligence-led investigations and effective prosecution of terror cases, an official statement said. The two-day event, held on November 19 and 20 at DRDO Bhawan here, was organised around the theme of 'Cross-Border Terrorism' and brought together senior officers of state police forces, central agencies and other stakeholders, it said. The conference was attended by 40 DGs/heads of state police and central agencies and 230 participants from anti-terror investigation units of the states, said the statement issued by the NIA. It was inaugurated by Shah in the presence of Minister of State for Home Bandi Sanjay Kumar, Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, senior officers of central and state agencies and other dignitaries. title: ICJ verdict noted; India consistently supported speedy return of Rohingya people: MEA
excerpt: New Delhi, Nov 20 (PTI): A day after the UN's top court ruled that Myanmar "committed genocide" against the Rohingya group in 2017, India on Friday said it has "taken note of the verdict" and asserted that New Delhi "consistently supported" the safe, speedy and sustainable return of the displaced Rohingya people from Rakhine state. At his bi-weekly media briefing, Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal was asked to comment on the historic judgment by the International Court of Justice (ICJ). "On the ICJ verdict… we have taken note of the verdict. India has consistently supported safe, speedy and sustainable return of the displaced Rohingya people from the Rakhine state," Jaiswal said. "To this end, India had earlier, as you would be aware, supported Rohingya camps in Bangladesh with relief supplies in five tranches under Operation Insaniyat. We have also supported the Rakhine State Development Programme in Myanmar for this purpose," he added. The International Court of Justice on Thursday ruled that Myanmar "committed genocide" against the Rohingya in the northern Rakhine state during the 2017 "clearance operations", in violation of its obligations under the Genocide Convention. The top UN court also ordered the Southeast Asian nation to allow the tens of thousands of people who fled the violence to return home. The case against Myanmar concerning alleged violations of the Genocide Convention was brought by The Gambia in November, 2019. ICJ President Yuji Iwasawa said the court, in a 9-6 decision, found that Myanmar "has committed genocide against the Rohingya group in northern Rakhine state, in violation of its obligations under the Genocide Convention". Bangladesh, which hosts over one million Rohingya refugees, welcomed the judgment, describing it as a significant development for justice and resolving the protracted refugee crisis. Most of the Rohingya refugees fled Myanmar's Rakhine state to evade persecution after a 2017 army crackdown in their homeland. Jaiswal was also asked how India viewed the recent meeting of the leaders from Russia, China, and the US, who sat for a trilateral summit in Shenzhen, China. "So, we have taken note of this meeting between the three APEC member countries. We await a fuller accounting of the concrete outcomes of the meeting before offering our assessment. So, that is what we have to say," he said. Another query was related to the recent Quad Summit held in Manila. The summit seemed to have been hosted by the US in Manila. Does this mean that India has now "relinquished its chairmanship, presidency of the Quad", and that there will not be a Quad Summit in India in the near future, or does India still hope to host a Quad Summit over here, a reporter asked. "We had the Quad Summit in Manila, and the four leaders of the Quad member countries met. We issued a statement, which you would have seen. There were some concrete outcomes which came out of it, including a Quad Business Leaders Forum, which is to be held next year, I think. "Also on emerging technologies, AI, maritime surveillance, on cable connectivity in the region, on several of these issues, including cybersecurity cooperation, and on security matters. So, the statement of the leaders is very clear that all these items, these decisions are practical cooperation, delivering good for people and countries in the Indo-Pacific region. In so far as the question of chairmanship is concerned, let me come back to you with details on that," he added. Jaiswal, when asked about some statements coming out of the US Commission of International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) levelling allegations against the Indian government in connection with voter rolls, said, "On USCIRF, I want to repeat what I have said earlier that we see it as a biased organisation with a blatantly political agenda, and I don't think an organisation which is so prejudiced needs to be taken seriously."
